1.sofaString: 107	Pt, ****** *******, is a 2 year-old female with dilated cardiomyopathy, referred by ******** *******, ****, Transplant Coordinator, for Psychosocial Assessment for Heart Transplant Evaluation.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the patient's mother, ****** ****, patient's father, ****** ******* and review of the medical records. SW spent approximately 60 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  **, ******, lives with her mother, father, *********, and *********'s spouse in ************, *******. They reside at **** ***** ***** ****, ************, ** *****. They live in * 4-bedroom home with central heating and a/c. The home is owned by ******'s *********, ***** *******.  They change the air filter monthly. They have city water. There is no smoking in the home.       Demographics:  Mother:  ****** ****  ***:  **/**/****  Language: French Creole, English  Education Level: AS degree, registered nurse  Employment:  Stay at home mom  Phone:  ***-***-****     Father:  ****** *******  DOB:  **/**/****  Language: French Creole, English  Education Level: High School Diploma  Employment:  Self-employed, **** and ***** electronics  Phone:  ***-***-****     Social History and Support Systems:  ******'s family is currently residing with ******'s ********* and her spouse. Prior to moving last month they were residing with family in *****. Mom reports that they moved to be closer to better hospitals. ******'s ********* is also an RN and provides support to the family. The extended family resides in ***** and ***** and will only be able to provide limited support.   Mom reports that ****** is on track developmentally. The pediatrician has not had any concerns. There is no history of PT/OT/ST involvement. ****** has not been in daycare since getting sick in ********. Mom plans to keep her home until she is better. She does not want to put her in ****. She is familiar with **** during her time as a home health nurse and feels that the children too often get sick there and does not want to expose ****** to illnesses.   Mom will be ******'s primary caregiver post-transplant. She does not have plans to return to work until ****** is better. Dad is self-employed and sets his own schedule. He will be available to assist as needed. Mom and ********* are both registered nurses. Mom has been doing ******'s PICC dressing changes when needed as well as managing her infusions.   Parents deny any objections to blood products, transfusions, etc.     Course of illness:     Mom reports that ****** was healthy prior to illness beginning in ********. ****** had several episodes of flu like symptoms that would come and go for several weeks. She was not seen by her pediatrician during those episodes but was evaluated during one of her brother's appointments and was noted to have a murmur. She was referred to cardiologist who admitted her to local hospital and diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy. She was evaluated by *** ******** ******** and placed on waiting list for heart transplant. She was also placed on outpatient IV Milrinone. In ****, a heart became available for ******. The family declined offer due to planned move to Jacksonville and not feeling that ****** was sick enough for transplant.   She is now admitted to ** ****** ****** due to needing PICC line replacement and Milrinone re-start.     Financial situation:  Patient's father provides the sole income for the family. He makes approximately $2000/month. Their expenses are limited as they are living with ******'s *********. Mom does not plan to return to work. They are not interested in applying for disability at this time. They are planning to purchase a home in the next year and feel that this would harm their **** application. SW encouraged them to speak with mortgage broker and consider, as it will help the family financially. SW provided family with information on ****.  ****** is covered by CMS Medicaid. This will cover all medical expenses at 100%.           The family has one vehicle. They deny that transportation will be a barrier for the family.     Family History:  Mom denies any DCF history, substance abuse, or mental history in the family.      Adherence:  Prior to moving in **** to ************, *** ******** had an offer for a heart for ******. They family declined due to planned moving in a few days as well as not feeling that ****** was sick enough for transplant. Per the hospital, it was also reported that mom would only provide team with her cell phone and they were unable to reach her to notify of the offer. They had to send law enforcement out to the home. Mom reports that they did not ask for any further contact information. She has provided ****** with contact information for herself, dad, and *********.      Assessment and recommendations:  Mom has expressed that they do not feel that ****** is sick enough to indicate transplant at this time. They have consented to listing but not to accepting an offer if one becomes available. The psychosocial concerns for this family are as follows: The family has indicated that they do not feel ****** is medically ready for transplant. The family's unwillingness to apply for social security disability to assist with the costs of transplant. The documentation from *** ******** stating that they had to send law enforcement to the home to notify of heart offer because they were unable to reach the family. SW is also concerned that mom never sought out medical treatment when ****** was sick with flu like symptoms for over a month. The murmur was only found due to pediatrician's insistence in evaluating her at her brother's appointment.        IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1     Family Background & Social Support -  2     Financial/Insurance - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence -3     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 1     Total:  14 Low/Moderate     The family scores as low/moderate risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.          Recommendations:  *Complete pre/post-transplant contracts to address concerns about adherence.  *Provide continuing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  *Offer support and guidance to family as needed.  *Provide encouragement for family to apply for social security disability.     ******** *****, MSW  Pediatric Heart and Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****
